info.title: Bitlync API
info.description:
Canonical read + act surface over the connected MSP stack. Writes are real; test them in the sandbox. Every write takes an idempotency_key (replay never duplicates). Fan-out writes return an explicit per-target envelope — partial is a first-class outcome. Every tenant-scoped response carries a top-level `sandbox` boolean: true means the tenant's connected stack is simulated (fixture-backed sandbox), false means production — simulated data is never mistakable for real.

**Grant keys** (connect UI, MSP permissions, this contract): `psa.company.read`, `psa.company.update`, `psa.company.field.create`, `psa.company.events`, `psa.contact.read`, `psa.contact.create`, `psa.ticket.read`, `psa.ticket.create`, `psa.ticket.update`, `psa.ticket.events`, `psa.time.write`, `psa.agreement.read`, `psa.agreement.line.write`, `psa.project.read`, `psa.project.write`, `psa.project.create`, `psa.opportunity.write`, `psa.config.read`, `psa.config.write`, `rmm.device.read`, `rmm.device.events`, `rmm.device.write`, `docs.document.read`, `docs.document.write`, plus existing `commerce` read/write. `never.delete`, `never.setup_tables`, `psa.company.create` and `psa.agreement.create` always refuse: vendors never create PSA companies, agreements or billing lines; `psa.agreement.line.write` only updates quantities on existing PSA lines the vendor matched (via the mapping API). A write without the grant returns `grant_missing` with `needed`, one English sentence, and `doc_url`. Leftover `psa_company_update_refused` means the grant is present and policy still refused.

**Escape hatch:** Canonical first. Every canonical object includes `vendor: {connector, native_id, native}` on reads (`native` is the raw vendor object; `.raw` is the same payload). `.raw` and `vendor.native` are read-only extra fields. Writes accept optional `vendor_native` after the write grant on tickets and on `POST /companies/write` (company custom fields; grant `psa.company.update`, default off). We do not guarantee every native field.

**Developer docs:** [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) · [Billing](/docs/billing) · [Alerts](/docs/alerts) · [Object dictionary](/docs/object-dictionary) · [What we write](/docs/object-dictionary#what-we-write) · [Error codes](/docs/errors) · Try it out below (paste your sandbox API key into Authorize).

get.description:
Canonical tickets from the tenant's PSA (synced_at + raw included).
Each ticket also includes `vendor: {connector, native_id, native}`
where `native` is the raw vendor object (same payload as read-only
`.raw`). Canonical first. Native escape hatch. We do not guarantee
every native field. Store-served with `last_synced_at` where a sync
engine is wired; `?live=true` is the explicit freshness escape hatch
— it re-syncs this request against the per-connection vendor budget.
Paginated: at most `limit` tickets (default 100, max 500) plus
`next_cursor` — pass it back as `cursor` for the next page; null
means this page is the last.

post.description:
Send one alert. Bitlync routes it to the MSP's destination.

Body: type (name or id), severity (optional; defaults to the type's
suggested severity), device ({id, name} or a string), customer,
description (optional), dry_run (default false), event_id or
idempotency_key. The id is unique per event. A repeat needs a new
id. The stored key is alert-event:{tenant}:{isv}:{event_id}.
A commit without either id returns 422 request_invalid. The ticket
title carries type, category, and severity. Repeat alerts for the
same device update one open ticket when the MSP left dedupe on.
Bitlync never reopens a ticket the MSP closed. Refused with
feature_off before any vendor call when alerts are disabled.
